verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The phone rings twice in an empty house and then stops.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles on the windowsill, undisturbed—
someone forgot to close the gate again,
and the goats have found the garden.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Steam rises from a cup no one will drink—
the kettle knew to stop
before the whistle woke the block.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left the porch light burning all night—
a moth gave up and settled on the bulb,
wings folded like a letter never sent.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Morning finds the mail still in the box—
rain-soft, addresses blurring into rivers,
a name no longer answering to itself.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The neighbor's radio hums through the fence—
a station no one tunes anymore,
playing static to the tomatoes.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The garden gate swings on its rusted hinge—
someone's boot prints stop halfway across the lawn,
already filling up with snow.

verses.author: model_B
model_A
verses.text:
The kettle forgets it was ever asked to sing—
I pour the cold water out anyway,
watch it disappear into the thirsty grass.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left their gloves on the fence post—
I don't touch them, don't call out,
just note how the frost has kept their shape.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The dog barks once at nothing, then stops—
I stand at the window a long while,
counting the seconds it takes silence to settle back.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A neighbor's radio drifts through the wall,
half a song I almost remember—
I let the words stay wrong, hum it my own way.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light flickers, decides to stay on—
moths arrive like they were always coming,
small and sure of what they love.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Steam rises off the coffee I forgot—
I drink it lukewarm anyway,
not everything needs saving while it's hot.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The mail comes late, just a flyer and a bill—
I read the flyer twice,
grateful for something that asks nothing back.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A crack runs through the kitchen tile,
been there since we moved in—
I stopped seeing it as broken years ago.
